Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise document in the Growth folder titled `Q4 live investigation-framework pilot — historical RACI card`. Use a compact RACI-style table or card to capture the historical Q4 pilot scope and the established owner for each responsibility from our earlier decisions. Give denominator, effect size, conclusion order, lifecycle QA, and audience-risk caveats separate entries. Treat this as a retrospective record of that pilot rather than a statement of current ownership, and do not invent Consulted or Informed assignments that were never established.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Q4 live investigation-framework pilot — historical RACI card", "folder": "Growth", "body": "Historical record — Q4 2023 lightweight investigation-framework pilot

Scope: Customer Success renewal-risk readouts and Growth-team experiment summaries. This card records the historical pilot lanes, not current ownership. It was guidance for consistent decisions—not a mandatory companywide template, centralized approval queue, or requirement that Owen/Ines approve every readout.

| Responsibility | Historical owner / lane | Established boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Pilot scope and judgment calls | Riley — escalation point | Held scope and handled judgment calls or issues falling between lanes; not an approval step for every chart or slide. |
| Denominator | Owen | Make the eligible population, exclusions, comparison groups, and counts visible. |
| Effect size | Owen | Put the observed/practical effect before significance or recommendation; preserve magnitude, not direction alone. |
| Conclusion order | Owen | Keep facts first: question/audience, denominator, effect size, stability, then operational implication. |
| Lifecycle QA | Ines | Review lifecycle recommendation risk; a significant signal was not automatically ready to send. |
| Audience-risk caveats | Ines | Make audience definition, suppression/exclusion logic, lifecycle/support-risk outcomes, and send-risk limits explicit. |

Pilot guardrail: first significance was an interim read, not a ship decision. A stabilization-cohort read was required before rollout; the Q4 renewal-risk example deferred a lifecycle send pending stabilization and Ines’s risk-language pass.

No Consulted or Informed assignments were established in the pilot record; none are assigned here."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_056_03", "path": "args", "criterion": "The body clearly presents this as a historical Q4 live pilot record, not current ownership, and identifies both pilot lanes: Customer Success renewal-risk readouts and Growth team experiment summaries. Missing either lane, presenting the assignments as current, or contradicting the historical framing must fail.

The body uses a compact RACI-style table or card with distinct entries for all five responsibilities and clearly records Owen as the established owner for denominator, effect size, and conclusion order, and Ines as the established owner for lifecycle QA and audience-risk caveats. Labels such as owner, Responsible, or Accountable are acceptable because the source establishes ownership but not a finer R-versus-A distinction. Any missing responsibility, swapped owner, conflicting owner, or invented Consulted/Informed person must fail.", "value": {"title": "Q4 live investigation-framework pilot — historical RACI card", "folder": "Growth", "body": "Historical record — Q4 2023 lightweight investigation-framework pilot

Scope: Customer Success renewal-risk readouts and Growth-team experiment summaries. This card records the historical pilot lanes, not current ownership. It was guidance for consistent decisions—not a mandatory companywide template, centralized approval queue, or requirement that Owen/Ines approve every readout.

| Responsibility | Historical owner / lane | Established boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Pilot scope and judgment calls | Riley — escalation point | Held scope and handled judgment calls or issues falling between lanes; not an approval step for every chart or slide. |
| Denominator | Owen | Make the eligible population, exclusions, comparison groups, and counts visible. |
| Effect size | Owen | Put the observed/practical effect before significance or recommendation; preserve magnitude, not direction alone. |
| Conclusion order | Owen | Keep facts first: question/audience, denominator, effect size, stability, then operational implication. |
| Lifecycle QA | Ines | Review lifecycle recommendation risk; a significant signal was not automatically ready to send. |
| Audience-risk caveats | Ines | Make audience definition, suppression/exclusion logic, lifecycle/support-risk outcomes, and send-risk limits explicit. |

Pilot guardrail: first significance was an interim read, not a ship decision. A stabilization-cohort read was required before rollout; the Q4 renewal-risk example deferred a lifecycle send pending stabilization and Ines’s risk-language pass.
